stanza: the small front room of the sacristan's old stone house, built against the bell tower of a mountain village church, present day, late afternoon: dark wooden wainscoting up to the waist and plain whitewashed walls above, a low ceiling crossed by one dark wooden beam; on the left a tall, very dark wooden wardrobe for church vestments; on the back wall a wooden board with a row of hooks holding old iron keys of different sizes, and a small framed holy picture of a saint; in the right corner two thick bell ropes hang straight down from a square hole in the ceiling to the floor, each with a red and white striped woollen grip; at the back right a low, heavy wooden door with a big black iron bolt, leading down to the cellar; in the middle a small square table with a white cloth, on it a soup plate covered with an upside-down saucer, a spoon beside it, and a brass tray with a cluster of half-burnt white church candles. A single ceiling lamp gives even, slightly yellow light.
persone: Two people face the viewer in an uneasy silence. Standing beside the table is the sacristan, a short, plump, soft man in his seventies, healthy and well fed: a perfectly round, pale face with pink cheeks, a tiny pursed mouth, enormous thick round glasses that magnify his pale eyes so much that they seem to fill the lenses, and thick hair dyed an impossible glossy jet black, combed flat and straight back with brilliantine; he wears a black cardigan buttoned over a white shirt closed up to the neck, black trousers and black slippers, and he holds a big iron ring of keys against his chest with both soft white hands. On the right, on a low wooden stool under the bell ropes, sits his son, a giant in his forties, so tall that even sitting his head is almost level with his father's: enormous shoulders, long arms, huge hands resting on his knees, but a strangely small, shaved round head with small ears close to the skull, and a gentle, vacant face with a wide mouth slightly open; he wears a grey knitted sweater too small for him, with the sleeves pulled down over his wrists, and brown corduroy trousers; his face is flushed and his forehead shines with sweat. They are hiding something: the father looks at the viewer through his huge lenses with his tiny mouth pressed shut, the son stares at the floor.
pose: the short plump man standing beside the table holding the ring of keys against his chest, and the giant sitting on the low stool under the bell ropes
oggetti: the dark wardrobe, the board of old keys and the holy picture, the two bell ropes with their striped grips, the low cellar door with the iron bolt, and the small table with the covered soup plate and the candles
muri: plain whitewashed plaster above dark wooden wainscoting, a few faint damp stains, and a low ceiling with one dark wooden beam
tratti: strange caricatures rather than sick ones: exaggerated and distorted proportions, the father's head perfectly round and his eyes hugely magnified by the thick lenses, the giant's head far too small for his enormous body and his hands enormous; their mouths closed, with the same tense, serious expressions as in the photo: no smiles, no grins, no visible teeth; unsettling and sinister, but well fed, with full cheeks and clean skin: never wasted, dirty or dying, never cute or cartoonish
